title: Ordinary scalar restriction under the constructed coefficient transport
statement: For a scheme morphism g:Y→X and a homomorphism f:B→R of arbitrary commutative rings in the site universe, restriction along g⁻¹(f_X) followed by relativeFiniteModelModules(g,B) is naturally isomorphic to relativeFiniteModelModules(g,R) followed by restriction along the actual constant coefficient map f on the small pro-etale model of Y. This compares ordinary module-sheaf functors; it has no derived, finiteness or local-constancy hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 03CY and 03D8; sites.tex Tag 03A0, equivalence of sites

proof.text: Naturality of the canonical inverse-image constant-section map follows from its adjunction and the sheafification unit. It holds for arbitrary commutative rings. Combine its inverse naturality with the constantSheafSheafCongrIso naturality to obtain the coefficient square for relativeFiniteModelCoefficient.

The two composite module functors have the same additive sections and restriction maps. The identity maps are linear by the coefficient square, so they and their inverses define componentwise module isomorphisms. Their naturality is the identity on each section.

theorem relativeFiniteScalarRestriction {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ X)
    {B R : Type (u + 1)} [CommRing B] [CommRing R] (f : B →+* R) :
    Nonempty ((pbcRestrict ((adicTowerInverseImage g).map
        ((constantSheaf (ProEt.topology X) CommRingCat.{u + 1}).map
          (CommRingCat.ofHom f))) ⋙ relativeFiniteModelModules g B) ≅
      (relativeFiniteModelModules g R ⋙ CategoryTheory.ConstantCompletion.res
        ((constantSheaf (proEtaleModelTopology Y) CommRingCat.{u + 1}).map
          (CommRingCat.ofHom f))))
